title: Phase-conditioned intrinsic gap and inter-phase capacity split
question: Can the intrinsic kinetic graph be decomposed into within-phase coercivity and inter-phase capacity, so a broken-sector gap is not confused with a global tunnelling mode?

new_perspective.principle: Separate local phase coercivity from the cross-phase bottleneck before attempting a thermodynamic Poincare transfer.
route: Sort the one-site q spectrum and define lower and upper physical-coordinate sectors, leaving a possible central level as neutral mass rather than silently assigning it to a phase.
For each conditional law pi, compute the full momentum graph gap and the induced lower/upper sector gaps using the same conductance c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi).
Record the cross-sector conductance K_cross=sum_{i in minus,j in plus} c_ij and the neutral mass as separate bottleneck data.
Stress beta and volume/cutoff rows while retaining the full-gap profile; a phasewise theorem may use the induced gaps even when a global gap is controlled by a phase-switching mode.
Use p-to-q and cross-edge deletion mutations as structural hostile tests: the diagonal q operator must have no kinetic edges, and deleting cross edges must expose disconnected phase blocks.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: An analytic lower bound for the induced sector graph on a phase-conditioned Hamiltonian core could feed the broken-sector GNS coercivity gate, while the cross-sector capacity identifies the separate phase-selection debt. The finite split is not a phase theorem.

finite_theorem.full_gap: lambda_full is the first positive eigenvalue of diag(pi)^(-1/2)Ldiag(pi)^(-1/2)
finite_theorem.sector_gaps: lambda_minus and lambda_plus are the first positive eigenvalues of the induced sector graphs with pi restricted and renormalized
finite_theorem.cross_capacity: K_cross=sum_{i in minus,j in plus} c_ij
finite_theorem.neutral_mass: m_0=sum_{q-levels not assigned to either sector} pi_i
finite_theorem.analytic_target: Prove a phase-conditioned sector gap on a common core and separately control the cross-sector capacity or phase boundary condition before invoking a broken-sector GNS gap.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks scalar nonnegativity and finite phase-partition bookkeeping only; spectra, Gibbs rows, phase limits and operator domains remain executable/open analysis.

promotion_criteria: Prove a cutoff-, volume- and phase-conditioned lower bound for both induced sector gaps on one Hamiltonian common core.
Control the neutral level and cross-sector capacity under source, boundary and exhaustion limits, or impose an explicit phase boundary condition with a proved selection theorem.
Only then combine the sector coercivity with the R-399 shell and the abstract GNS transfer gate.
stop_conditions: If an induced sector gap collapses under a validated cutoff or volume stress, retain the phase split only as a diagnostic and do not claim phasewise coercivity.
If cross-sector capacity is the smallest scale, keep the global gap separate from the within-phase gap and require a phase-selection argument.
Finite sector positivity and finite capacity are not a common-core, broken-sector, QFT or mass-gap theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite phase-conditioned intrinsic-graph stress only. It proves no uniform sector gap, phase selection, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The split is a bookkeeping and stress-test interface: it identifies separate within-phase and cross-phase quantities without promoting either finite profile to a thermodynamic theorem.
